full_judgment: But the evidence has to be taken with great caution and in a number of cases it has been held that although an accomplice's evidence is sufficient to prove the prosecution case yet in each case the special feature and facts have to be taken into consideration. Section 133 of the Evidence Act must be read with illustration (b) to section 144 as both deal with the same subject It has been long a rule of practice that it is dangerous to convict an accused on the uncorroborated testimony of an accomplice. Although, according to section 133, the testimony of an accomplice is admissible and a conviction based on the uncorroborated testimony of an accomplice is not illegal yet it is highly dangerous to base a conviction on such evidence alone and the court almost invariably starts with the presumption against the trustworthiness of the accomplice and unless the circumstances are quite exceptional the court refuses to convict on the uncorroborated evidence of an accomplice. Of course, where the court is satisfied about the trustworthiness of the accomplice's testimony is shall not refrain itself from convicting the accused upon suchuncorroborated testimony of the accomplice. In this case PW 11 made statement before the Magistrate confessing his guilt under section 164 CrPC and we find from his confessional statement that Ator Ali severed the head of Babor Ali near the beel but before the trial Court he said that Babor Ali was killed earlier and Jilani dealt sora blow. He also in court stated Piar Miah called Babor Ali but in his statement under section 164 CrPC he did not state so. Thus we find contradictions between his statement under section 164 CrPC and the statement made before the court. In that view of his statements we hold that the evidence of accomplice PW 11 Sukur is not free from doubt Accomplice's evidence requires corroboration by other independent witnesses connecting the accused with the crime and this rule of caution has now assumed the character of rule of law although the evidence of an approver recorded under section 164 CrPC can be used for contradicting him under sections 145 and 155 of the Evidence Act or for corroborating his evidence under section 157 CrPC.
